# Open Health Sync

> Open Health Sync is an open source, self-hosted health data aggregator (AGPL-3.0) that collects data from wearables and health apps (Apple Health, Health Connect, Garmin, Oura, WHOOP, Fitbit, Withings, Polar, Strava, Dexcom and others, 18 sources) and serves it in one data model through a REST API, FHIR R4, Open mHealth, signed webhooks, CSV and Parquet exports and a read-only MCP server. It is one Go binary (`ohs`) plus PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB, and runs in Docker, on Kubernetes, on Linux and macOS or on a Raspberry Pi 5.

- Version 0.3.0, pre-1.0: any release may change the API, configuration or schema.
- Self-hosted alternative to hosted wearable APIs such as Terra; operators register their own developer app with each vendor.
- Not a medical device: it moves and stores readings, it does not interpret them.
- Homepage: https://openhealthsync.com. Repository: https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync

## Docs

- [Open Health Sync](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/README.md): Overview, features, quickstart, comparison with hosted APIs and FAQ.
- [API guide](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/api.md): Credentials, conventions, pagination, errors, connecting providers, uploads, reads, FHIR, Open mHealth and exports in one read.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): Open Health Sync is one Go binary, ohs, and one Postgres database with the TimescaleDB extension.
- [Self-hosting Open Health Sync](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md): Run it with Docker Compose: configuration, ohs doctor, images, Raspberry Pi, S3 raw store, upgrades, backups and rotating secrets.
- [Connectors](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/README.md): A connector teaches Open Health Sync one source.
- [Data model](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/data-model.md): Every canonical record, field and quantity name, with its unit, UCUM and LOINC codes (generated from internal/model).
- [FHIR R4 output](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/fhir.md): Open Health Sync serves a user's records as FHIR R4 (4.0.1) Observations, so a FHIR client, an EHR integration or a research pipeline can read them without learning the REST JSON shapes: quantity samples (heart rate, steps, weight, SpO2...), blood pressure readings, sleep sessions, workouts, daily summaries, ECG recordings with their waveform, and what the user ate and drank.
- [Open mHealth output](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/open-mhealth.md): Open Health Sync serves a user's records as Open mHealth data points, so a tool built on the Open mHealth schemas (a research pipeline, a mobile health study, an analysis notebook) can read them without learning the REST JSON shapes.
- [CSV and Parquet exports](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/exports.md): An export is one file holding every record of one list of a user in a time window: CSV for a spreadsheet, Parquet for a data pipeline (pandas, Polars, DuckDB, Spark, a warehouse).
- [Outgoing webhooks](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/webhooks.md): Instead of polling coverage, your server can be told when something changes.
- [MCP server](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/mcp.md): Open Health Sync speaks the Model Context Protocol, so an AI agent can read health data directly.
- [Client SDKs](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/sdks/README.md): Four client libraries call the REST API from an app: Kotlin, Swift, React Native and Flutter.
- [Server SDKs](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/server-sdks.md): Two clients of the API for your backend, the code that holds a tenant API key (ohs_sk_...): TypeScript (Node.js 18+) and Python (3.9+), generated from the OpenAPI file.
- [Background sync](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/background-sync.md): Open Health Sync keeps each user's data current without anyone pressing "sync".
- [Security model](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/security-model.md): This page states what Open Health Sync protects, from whom, how, and where it stops.
- [Consent](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/consent.md): Open Health Sync keeps each end user's consent per source and per data category: a user can share their sleep and activity from one wearable but not their heart data, and change their mind later.
- [Health data API questions](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/faq.md): Short answers to the questions developers ask most when they look for a way to collect wearable and health data.
- [Health data aggregators compared](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/compare/README.md): A health data aggregator collects data from wearables and health apps (Apple Health, Health Connect, Oura, WHOOP, Garmin, Fitbit, Withings and others) and gives your product one API for all of them, instead of one integration per vendor.
- [Terra API alternative](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/compare/terra.md): Open Health Sync is an open source, self-hosted alternative to the Terra API.
- [OpenAPI contract](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/api/openapi.yaml): The OpenAPI 3.1 contract of the REST API, the source of truth for every route.

## Guides

- [Import Apple Health data into PostgreSQL](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/apple-health-to-postgres.md): To export Apple Health data to PostgreSQL, run Open Health Sync and load the Health app export with ohs import apple-health: your history lands in Postgres as tables you can query with SQL.
- [Convert an Apple Health export to CSV](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/apple-health-to-csv.md): The Health app on the iPhone exports everything it holds as export.zip, but inside it is one large XML file (export.xml) that Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets cannot open as it is, often a few gigabytes once unzipped.
- [Connect Claude to your Apple Health data](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/apple-health-mcp.md): To use Apple Health data in Claude through MCP, load your Health app export into Open Health Sync and add its read-only MCP server to Claude with a token that can only read one person's data.
- [Sync HealthKit data from your iOS app to your own backend](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/healthkit-ios-app-sync.md): HealthKit has no server API, so your iOS app has to send the data out.
- [Send Android Health Connect data to your own server](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/health-connect-to-server.md): Health Connect has no server API, so the data has to leave from the phone: your Android app reads the records it was granted and uploads them as gzip NDJSON parts to POST /v1/ingest/health-connect on an Open Health Sync server you run.
- [Get Samsung Health data through an API](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/samsung-health-data.md): Samsung Health has no cloud API to pull from: its data lives on the phone.
- [Get Oura data as FHIR R4](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/oura-fhir.md): To get Oura data as FHIR R4, connect the ring to Open Health Sync and read its FHIR endpoints: sleep, heart rate, HRV, SpO2 and daily scores come back as FHIR Observations.
- [Export WHOOP data to CSV or Parquet](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/whoop-export.md): To get WHOOP data through an API, connect WHOOP to Open Health Sync with OAuth: it pulls your recovery, strain, sleep and workouts into a database you run, and exports them as CSV or Parquet at any time.
- [Export Withings weight and blood pressure to CSV or SQL](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/withings-export.md): The Withings app (Health Mate) can send you a one-off export of your measurements as CSV files.
- [Export Garmin Connect activities to PostgreSQL or CSV](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/garmin-export.md): Garmin Connect lets you download your whole account: every activity you ever synced, as the original FIT files.
- [Get Fitbit data through the Google Health API and export it](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/fitbit-export.md): To get Fitbit data through an API now, connect the Google Account that holds it to Open Health Sync: it pulls steps, heart rate, HRV, SpO2, sleep, workouts and body measurements from the Google Health API into a database you run, and exports them as CSV or Parquet at any time.
- [Export Polar data to CSV or PostgreSQL](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/polar-export.md): To export Polar data to CSV or PostgreSQL, connect your Polar Flow account to Open Health Sync through Polar's AccessLink API: it pulls exercises, sleep, Nightly Recharge, daily activity and continuous heart rate into a PostgreSQL database you run, and exports them as CSV or Parquet at any time.
- [Export Strava activities to PostgreSQL or CSV](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/strava-export.md): To export Strava activities to PostgreSQL or CSV, connect your Strava account to Open Health Sync with OAuth: it pulls each activity's summary (sport, start, duration, distance, speed, elevation, heart rate, energy) into a PostgreSQL database you run, as one workout row, and exports them as CSV or Parquet at any time.
- [Get Dexcom CGM glucose readings through an API](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/dexcom-glucose-api.md): To get Dexcom CGM glucose readings through an API, connect a Dexcom account to Open Health Sync with OAuth: it pulls the readings from the official Dexcom API v3 into a database you run, and serves them over a REST API, as CSV or Parquet, or as FHIR R4 Observations.
- [Export Xiaomi Mi Fitness data to CSV or PostgreSQL](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/mi-fitness-export.md): Xiaomi publishes no health API, but your Xiaomi account lets you download a copy of your Mi Fitness data.
- [Import FIT, GPX and TCX activity files into PostgreSQL](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/fit-gpx-tcx-import.md): ohs import files loads FIT, GPX and TCX files (one file, a folder or a whole account export zip) into the PostgreSQL database of an Open Health Sync server you run.
- [Record a Bluetooth heart rate strap, blood pressure cuff or scale without a phone](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/bluetooth-devices.md): Run ohs-bridge, the Open Health Sync desktop bridge, on a Mac, a Linux machine, a Raspberry Pi or a Windows PC near your devices.
- [Get a webhook when new wearable data arrives](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/webhooks-new-data.md): To be told when new wearable data arrives, register an endpoint with POST /v1/webhooks and subscribe to data.written: Open Health Sync posts a signed JSON event each time a sync or an upload writes new or changed records, naming the user, the provider and the days.
- [Export wearable data as Open mHealth JSON](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/open-mhealth-export.md): To get wearable data as Open mHealth JSON, call GET /v1/users/{id}/omh/data-points on Open Health Sync: it returns a user's records from every connected source as Open mHealth data points, each a header and a body that follows one schema of the Open mHealth catalog.
- [Give an AI agent read-only access to wearable data over MCP](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/mcp-remote-agent.md): To give an AI agent read-only access to wearable data, point it at the /mcp endpoint of your Open Health Sync instance with a bearer token: the agent gets tools such as get_daily, get_sleep and get_samples over every source the instance holds (Oura, WHOOP, Garmin, Withings, Apple Health and the rest), and no tool can write, delete or connect anything.
- [Share your health data with your clinician through a link](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/share-with-clinician.md): To share your health data with your clinician, make a share link in Open Health Sync: one call to POST /v1/users/{id}/shares picks the categories and the time window, and returns a link your clinician opens in a browser.
- [Combine data from several wearables without counting it twice](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/merge-multiple-wearables.md): Open Health Sync stores every source's records as received and, by default, reads them through a merged view (view=merged): a record is listed only when no better ranked source has a matching one, so a sum or an average counts nothing twice.
- [Run Open Health Sync with Docker Compose and HTTPS](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/docker-compose-https.md): To serve Open Health Sync over HTTPS, start it with deploy/docker-compose.yml, which publishes the API on 127.0.0.1:8080 only, and put Caddy in front with the bundled deploy/Caddyfile, which gets a TLS certificate on its own.
- [Self-host a health data API on a Raspberry Pi 5](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/raspberry-pi.md): A Raspberry Pi 5 with 4 GB of memory runs the whole Open Health Sync stack (the API, the sync workers and Postgres with TimescaleDB) with Docker Compose and one overlay file, deploy/docker-compose.pi.yml, that trims memory use.
- [Delete a user's health data (erasure and data portability)](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/delete-user-data.md): To erase a user in Open Health Sync, call DELETE /v1/users/{id}: it answers 202 with a job_id, cuts the user's access at once, and a background job removes their raw files, every record and the user.
- [Move from the Terra API to a self-hosted aggregator](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/migrate-from-terra.md): Open Health Sync is an open source, self-hosted aggregator you can move to from the Terra API: most Terra concepts have a direct counterpart.
- [Repair Fitbit rows of relayed Apple Health and Health Connect data](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/how-to/fitbit-relayed-points.md): A user who links Apple Health (or Health Connect) in the Google Health app gets that data back through the Fitbit connector, marked platform HEALTH_KIT (or HEALTH_CONNECT) in metadata.

## Optional

- [Activity files (FIT, GPX, TCX)](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/activity-files.md): Import FIT, GPX and TCX files from any device or app, with routes and per-second heart rate.
- [Apple Health connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/apple-health.md): Apple Health setup (developer app, keys, scopes), what is pulled and how it maps to the canonical model.
- [Bluetooth devices](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/bluetooth.md): Standard Bluetooth health profiles read by ohs-bridge or the Swift and Kotlin SDKs, decoded on the server.
- [COROS (research notes)](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/coros.md): There is no COROS connector yet.
- [Dexcom connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/dexcom.md): Dexcom setup (developer app, keys, scopes), what is pulled and how it maps to the canonical model.

- [intervals.icu connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/intervals-icu.md): intervals.icu setup (developer app, keys, scopes), what is pulled and how it maps to the canonical model.
- [OMRON connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/omron.md): OMRON setup (developer app, keys, scopes), what is pulled and how it maps to the canonical model.

- [Polar connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/polar.md): Polar setup (developer app, keys, scopes), what is pulled and how it maps to the canonical model.

- [Suunto connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/suunto.md): Suunto setup (developer app, keys, scopes), what is pulled and how it maps to the canonical model.
- [Ultrahuman connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/ultrahuman.md): Ultrahuman setup (developer app, keys, scopes), what is pulled and how it maps to the canonical model.
- [WHOOP connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/whoop.md): WHOOP setup (developer app, keys, scopes), what is pulled and how it maps to the canonical model.
- [Withings connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/withings.md): Withings setup (developer app, keys, scopes), what is pulled and how it maps to the canonical model.
- [Xiaomi connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/connectors/xiaomi.md): Xiaomi setup (developer app, keys, scopes), what is pulled and how it maps to the canonical model.
- [Junction alternative](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/compare/junction.md): Open Health Sync is an open source, self-hosted alternative to Junction, the health data API formerly called Vital.
- [Thryve alternative](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/compare/thryve.md): Open Health Sync is an open source, self-hosted alternative to Thryve, the wearable data API hosted in Germany.
- [Spike API alternative](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/compare/spike.md): Open Health Sync is an open source, self-hosted alternative to the Spike API.
- [Sahha alternative](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/compare/sahha.md): Sahha and Open Health Sync both collect data from wearables and health apps, but they stop at different places.
- [ROOK alternative](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/compare/rook.md): Open Health Sync is an open source, self-hosted alternative to ROOK for wearable data.
- [Deploy on Render, Fly.io or Railway](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/deploy-platforms.md): These templates run Open Health Sync on a hosting platform, without a server of your own.
- [Kubernetes with Helm](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/helm.md): The chart in deploy/helm/ohs runs Open Health Sync on Kubernetes.
- [Hardening checklist](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/hardening.md): What to set before an instance holds real people's health data.
- [Backup and restore](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/backup-and-restore.md): Two scripts back up and restore an install that runs on the bundled Docker Compose stack: scripts/backup.sh writes one archive, scripts/restore.sh puts it back.
- [Desktop bridge: `ohs-bridge`](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/bridge.md): ohs-bridge runs on a computer or a Raspberry Pi next to your devices.
- [Share links](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/share-links.md): A share link lets a person show some of their own data to someone they choose (a physician, a coach, a relative) without handing over a credential or a file.
- [Writing a connector](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/writing-a-connector.md): A connector teaches Open Health Sync one provider.
- [Build with your own health data](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/recipes/README.md): Your ring knows your sleep, your watch your heart rate, your phone your steps, and each keeps its share in its own app.
- [Learn by building](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/docs/learn/README.md): Seven small projects that take you from "my data is stuck in five apps" to tools of your own: a sleep report, an HRV trend, an AI assistant that reads your training, a dashboard, a message on your phone the morning your night syncs.
- [Open Health Sync: your own training, sleep and recovery data](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/skills/open-health-sync/SKILL.md): Open Health Sync gathers a person's data from their watch, ring, band, scale or the Health app into one place and serves it to agents through a read-only MCP server.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): All notable changes to Open Health Sync are listed here.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Set up, test, layout and rules for contributions; recording your own account as a test fixture.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/soma-intelligence/open-health-sync/blob/main/AGENTS.md): Notes for coding agents working in this repository.
